# MATE Documentation

> MATE is a self-hosted platform for process mining: it turns event logs into process models, performance figures, conformance results, and drift reports, and it treats every analysis as an installable module.

MATE is a self-hosted, modular process-mining platform. This file indexes the published manual: every chapter in reading order, grouped as in the site navigation. Links are relative to this file, which is served next to the chapter pages.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](introduction.html): MATE is a self-hosted platform for process mining: it turns event logs into process models, performance figures, conformance results, and drift reports, and it treats every analysis as an installable module.
- [Install and start](install-and-start.html): From a clean host to a logged-in workspace. The whole stack is one compose file.
- [Your first analysis](your-first-analysis.html): One log from import to dashboard: import it, monitor the jobs, open a module, and build a board.

## Using MATE

- [Importing event logs](importing-event-logs.html): The wizard accepts five format families, probes them server-side, and writes nothing until you confirm the interpretation.
- [Working with logs](working-with-logs.html): Filtering, editing, and organising logs after the first import.
- [Exploring a process](exploring-a-process.html): The process page is the workspace for one log. Its tabs are URL-backed, so any view — a filtered event list, a variant, an activity — is a shareable link.
- [Modules](modules.html): Modules are the platform's capabilities. The Modules page manages which ones your account has.
- [Jobs and the interface](jobs-and-the-interface.html): Every long operation is a job, and the interface reports them consistently.
- [Dashboards](dashboards.html): A dashboard is a canvas of cards from any module, scoped by one filter bar and shareable read-only.
- [MATE AI](mate-ai.html): The assistant runs in a right-hand panel: context-aware, restricted by a data wall, and configured per account.
- [Settings and admin](settings-and-admin.html): Settings are per user and stored server-side, so they follow the account across browsers. The Profile page holds the account itself.

## Module guides

- [Actor Performance](guide-actor-performance.html): Actor Performance explains why work waits between two steps of a case. For every step and its next step it classifies how the work moved between people: the same actor carried on, the same actor did something else in…
- [AgentSimulator](guide-agentsimulator.html): AgentSimulator learns from your log how the people and systems in your process work: who does which activity, when they work, how long it takes and who hands work to whom. It then generates synthetic logs of the proce…
- [Complexity](guide-complexity.html): Complexity puts numbers on how tangled your process is. It scores the log with entropy, size, variation and Pentland measures and lists them in two tables, so you can compare processes or process versions and see how…
- [Complexity Over Time](guide-complexity-over-time.html): Complexity Over Time shows whether your process is getting simpler or more tangled. It cuts the log into time slices, scores each slice with the measures of the Complexity module and plots the metrics you choose as a…
- [Complexity V2](guide-complexity-v2.html): Complexity V2 scores your log with a suite of 28 complexity metrics covering entropy, size, variation and the distance between cases, and draws the matrix of transition probabilities between activities. Use it to see…
- [Complexity V2 Over Time](guide-complexity-v2-over-time.html): Complexity V2 Over Time shows whether your process is getting simpler or more tangled, measured with the 28 metrics of Complexity V2. It cuts the log into time slices, scores each slice with the whole suite and plots…
- [Concept Drift Explainer](guide-concept-drift-explainer.html): Concept Drift Explainer looks for the reason behind a change that CV4CDD detected. You upload dated company documents, such as policies, announcements or slide decks. For a drift you choose, it finds the documents fro…
- [Conformance Checking](guide-conformance.html): Conformance Checking replays your event log against a reference BPMN model that you upload. You get the fitness and precision of the model, the share of cases that follow it, and the places where cases deviate, painte…
- [CV4CDD - Concept Drift Detection](guide-cv4cdd.html): CV4CDD finds out when your process changed. It turns the log into an image of how alike the process was in different periods and lets a trained image model mark the changes. You get a list of drifts with their type, t…
- [Discovery](guide-discovery.html): Discovery mines your event log into process models. It shows how cases actually run as a directly-follows graph (DFG), a Petri net, a process tree, a prefix tree, a heuristics net and a BPMN diagram, so you can see th…
- [Log Evolution](guide-log-evolution.html): Log Evolution shows how your log grows and shifts over time. You get case arrivals against completions, work in progress, the changing mix of activities and a dotted chart of the events, so you can spot backlogs, seas…
- [Object-Centric Discovery](guide-ocel-discovery.html): Object-Centric Discovery shows how a process runs when several kinds of objects, such as orders, items and invoices, take part in the same events. You get the object types, their directly-follows graphs, an object-cen…
- [Pcomp](guide-pcomp.html): Pcomp tests whether two event logs differ by more than chance. You pick a second log, run a permutation test or a bootstrap test, and get a p-value for the difference between the traces of the two logs.
- [Performance](guide-performance.html): Performance shows how fast your process runs and where cases lose time. You get throughput, cycle-time and lead-time figures, a histogram of how long cases take, and a table of the activities where cases spend unusual…
- [Performance Metrics (Java)](guide-performance-java.html): Performance Metrics (Java) shows where your process spends its time. You get the headline timing figures, a ranking of the activities by the time cases stay in them, and a ranking of the hand-offs between two activiti…
- [Performance Over Time](guide-performance-over-time.html): Performance Over Time shows whether your process is getting faster or slower. It cuts the log into time slices, calculates the Performance module's KPIs on each slice and plots the metrics you choose as a trend, with…
- [Process Comparison](guide-process-comparison.html): Process Comparison puts two views of event logs side by side and shows what differs: headline figures, similarity scores, an overlaid process map and diagram, the variants and the activities. Each side is a log plus i…
- [Temporal Mapper](guide-temporal-mapper.html): Temporal Mapper groups calendar periods (days, weeks, months or years) whose activity patterns look alike into states, then shows how the process moves between those states over time. Use it to see which patterns recu…

## Platform

- [Architecture and data](architecture.html): Services, state locations, and the path from an uploaded file to a queryable log.
- [Jobs, modules and isolation](jobs-modules-and-isolation.html): The job queue, the event bus, and the module system, for module authors and operators.
- [Security and privacy](security-and-privacy.html): The invariants that protect a deployment, and the controls on data leaving it.

## Module development

- [Your first module](your-first-module.html): A module is a folder with a manifest, a handler class, and optionally a frontend. Start from a bundled module, rename it, and make it compute something.
- [The manifest](the-manifest.html): manifest.yaml is the registration, the contract, and the documentation of a module. The SDK validates it locally; the loader validates it again at startup.
- [Handlers and the context](handlers-and-the-context.html): module.py holds one Module subclass with three kinds of handler, all receiving an injected ModuleContext.
- [Logs, jobs and results](logs-jobs-and-results.html): Reading the log, declaring long-running work, and storing results.
- [Module communication](module-communication.html): Modules never import each other. They communicate through two declared mechanisms and order themselves through one reserved topic.
- [Frontend: panels, widgets and datasets](frontend-panels-widgets-and-datasets.html): Frontends are TypeScript regardless of the backend language. The platform bundles them with esbuild into .dist/ at startup; the Next.js build never sees your sources, and a panel may only import the packages listed in…
- [Dependencies, isolation and runtimes](dependencies-isolation-and-runtimes.html): Where a module's code runs, and which libraries it can import.
- [Testing and publishing](testing-and-publishing.html): Module tests are ordinary pytest. The SDK deliberately ships no test double: the context is defined by Protocols, so a test fakes exactly what a handler touches.

## Interfaces

- [REST API](rest-api.html): Everything the app can do is available over HTTP. This chapter is the contract: the endpoint index below is complete, and /openapi.json owns the request and response shapes.
- [MCP server](mcp-server.html): The Model Context Protocol interface gives external AI clients scoped access to the same platform. It is opt-in, and its limits are enforced structurally rather than by prompt instructions.

## Operate

- [Deployment](deployment.html): Two deployments are supported: a local stack on one machine, and a production deployment behind a proxy with TLS. Both use the same compose file plus an overlay.
- [Configuration](configuration.html): Every knob a running platform reads. The deployment variables — URLs, identity, storage, MCP, tracking — are documented with inline commentary in .env.example; the job and compute knobs below are read from the environ…
- [Backup, storage and limits](backup-and-storage.html): Three stores hold state: the metadata database, the filesystem (or the bucket), and the Keycloak volume.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html): Symptoms by area, with the cause that most often explains them.

## Project

- [Contributing and development](contributing.html): Four contribution paths: ship a module, report a bug, improve this manual, or work on the platform.
